in_english.name: Ephraim
in_english.long_meaning: From the Hebrew, meaning 'fruitful' or 'double fruitful' or 'two fish', and derived from the root 'aphar' which means 'to bear fruit'.

biblical_reference.note: The second son of Joseph and Asenath, born in Egypt. Ephraim and his brother Manasseh were adopted by Jacob as his sons.

saint_reference.note: Ephraim is not a recognized Christian saint name.

data.spiritual_significance: In Jewish tradition, the name Ephraim is believed to have deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the idea of adoption. Joseph adopted Ephraim and Manasseh, and their namesake became synonymous with the idea of being taken in and accepted into a new family or community. In this vein, the name Ephraim can represent the idea of inclusion, acceptance, and the ability to start anew. Additionally, the name Ephraim is also connected to the name El-Phraim, which means "God the father of Phraim," further emphasizing the idea of God's love, protection, and nurturing care for the Israelites.

It refers to the double fruit of the womb, representing the two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, whom Joseph adopted as his own. In Christianity, this name has a unique significance as a reminder of God's blessings and promises. This article provides a comprehensive understanding of the name Ephrayim, its cultural and religious usage, and its appeal to parents.
